topics.title: Sets, Surds, Binary Operations, and Logical Reasoning

subtopics.content: Set properties, Venn diagrams, De Morgan's laws, surd operations, rationalization, binary operation properties, logic truth tables
subtopics.objective: Solve set problems involving union, intersection, complements, and Venn diagrams[cite: 320]; simplify, manipulate, and rationalize surd denominators[cite: 320, 321]; apply closure, commutativity, associativity, identity, and inverse to binary operations[cite: 321]; construct truth tables to evaluate compound logical statements and implications[cite: 321].

topics.title: Functions, Polynomials, Rational Functions, Indices, and Logarithms

subtopics.content: Mapping types, composite/inverse functions, linear/quadratic/cubic functions, quadratic inequalities, polynomial remainder/factor theorems, partial fractions, laws of indices and logarithms
subtopics.objective: Determine domains, ranges, inverse, and composite functions[cite: 321]; sketch and solve linear, quadratic, and cubic functions/equations[cite: 321, 322]; apply factor and remainder theorems to polynomials[cite: 322, 323]; resolve rational functions into partial fractions[cite: 323]; solve exponential and logarithmic equations including change of base and linear reduction ($y=ax^b$)[cite: 323, 324].

topics.title: Permutations, Combinations, Binomial Theorem, Sequences & Series, Matrices, and Linear Transformations

subtopics.content: Arrangements and selections ($^nP_r, ^nC_r$), binomial expansions, AP/GP sequences, infinite series, matrix operations, determinants, inverse matrices, linear transformations
subtopics.objective: Solve arrangement and combination problems[cite: 324]; expand binomial expressions for positive integral indices[cite: 324]; calculate terms and sums of AP, GP, recurrence, and infinite series[cite: 324, 325]; perform matrix operations, evaluate $2\times2$ and $3\times3$ determinants, find inverses, and apply matrices to linear transformations and geometry[cite: 325, 326].

subtopics.content: Trigonometric ratios/identities, compound/multiple angles, graphs, coordinate geometry of lines and conic sections (circles, parabolas), differentiation rules, maxima/minima, indefinite/definite integrals, area/volume applications
subtopics.objective: Prove trigonometric identities and solve equations involving compound/multiple angles[cite: 326, 327]; analyze line gradients, midpoints, acute angles, perpendicular distances, circles, and parabola equations[cite: 327, 328]; differentiate polynomials, trigonometric, and transcendental functions using chain/product/quotient rules[cite: 328, 329]; determine turning points, tangents, normals, and kinematics[cite: 329]; evaluate indefinite/definite integrals to compute plane areas, volumes of revolution, and trapezium rule approximations[cite: 329, 330].

subtopics.content: Data representation, measures of location and dispersion, scatter diagrams, correlation coefficients, regression lines, sample spaces, probability laws, binomial and Poisson distributions
subtopics.objective: Construct frequency tables, histograms, and cumulative frequency curves (Ogives)[cite: 330]; calculate mean, median, mode, variance, and standard deviation for grouped/ungrouped data[cite: 330, 331]; plot scatter diagrams, calculate Spearman's rank correlation, and find lines of best fit[cite: 331]; compute classical, conditional, mutually exclusive, and independent probabilities[cite: 331]; apply Binomial and Poisson probability distributions[cite: 331].

subtopics.content: Vector algebra, unit/position vectors, scalar (dot) products, coplanar forces, equilibrium, Lami's theorem, moments, friction, kinematics equations, Newton's laws, impulse, momentum, and projectiles
subtopics.objective: Perform vector addition, scalar multiplication, unit vector calculations, and scalar dot products[cite: 331, 332, 333]; resolve coplanar forces, apply Lami's theorem, moments, and friction principles to bodies in equilibrium[cite: 333]; solve rectilinear motion problems using equations of motion, Newton's laws, momentum conservation, and projectile trajectories[cite: 334].
